'''Melvin Lax'''  (March 8, 1922 – December 8, 2002) was a distinguished professor of physics at [[City College of New York]]<ref>{{cite journal|author1=Alfano, Robert R. |author2-link=Herman Z. Cummins |author2=Cummins, Herman Z. |author3-link=Myriam Sarachik |author3=Sarachik, Myriam |author4=Birman, Joseph L. |title=Obituary: Melvin Lax|journal=Physics Today|date=May 2003|volume=56|issue=5|pages=78–79|doi=10.1063/1.1583545|bibcode = 2003PhT....56e..78A |author1-link=Robert Alfano |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>[https://www.nytimes.com/2002/12/21/classified/paid-notice-deaths-lax-melvin.html?scp=1&sq=professor%20MELVIN%20LAX&st=cse paid CUNY obituary in ''The New York Times'', Paid Notice: Deaths LAX, MELVIN December 24, 2022]</ref> and elected a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 1983.<ref name="NAP">[http://www.nap.edu/openbook.php?record_id=11522&page=270 National Academies Press, V.87-2006]</ref> He did research on random processes in physics.<ref>[http://www.oup.com/us/catalog/general/subject/Physics/Mathematicalphysics/?view=usa&ci=9780198567769 Oxford University Press:Random Processes in Physics and Finance]</ref> Lax was the chairman of the [[Theoretical Physics]] Department at [[Bell Labs]] from 1962 to 1964.<ref name="NAP"/> He was also a Fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]], the [[American Physical Society]], the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]], and the [[Optical Society of America]].<ref name="NAP"/>

== Academic life ==
Lax received his B.A. in physics from [[New York University]] ([[Latin honors|summa cum laude]]) in 1942, and M.S. and Ph.D. from [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in 1943 and 1947, respectively. He was a professor at [[Syracuse University]] (1947 to 1955). Subsequently, Lax joined the new Theory Department at [[Bell Laboratories]] in [[Murray Hill, New Jersey]] in 1955. He worked first as a member of the technical staff from 1955 to 1962, as then as chairman of the theoretical physics department from 1962 to 1964. Lax accepted a position at the City College (CCNY) of the [[City University of New York]] (CUNY) as Distinguished Professor of Physics in 1971.<ref name="NAP"/>

== Awards ==
Lax was awarded the [[Willintwix]] Medal for [[Laser science|Laser Science]] and [[Quantum Optics]] in 1999.<ref name="NAP"/><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.lambmedal.org/ |title=The Willis E. Lamb Award for Laser Science and Quantum Optics |access-date=2011-12-17 |archive-date=2016-03-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305091517/http://www.lambmedal.org/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>
